scenes.visual: Title card 'Two Kinds of Zero' over a single pond at dusk with three empty tick boxes beneath it. Reuse the first film's COLOUR MAP: OCCUPIED pond = filled TEAL; EMPTY pond = GREY outline; GOLD = colonization; RED tick = local extinction; symbol p = fraction occupied. New for this film: a visit is a small tick box reading 1 (detected, TEAL fill) or 0 (not detected, white); a pond that is occupied but undetected is drawn TEAL with a dashed outline and a cartoon toad hidden in reeds. Naive counts are GREY bars; corrected estimates TEAL bars. Cream background, 16:9. Every number appears as on-screen text. Expected tallies are computed and labelled 'computed'; anything else is 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: Sources, rescue and corridors all rest on one record: which ponds are occupied. Three visits, no toads heard. Is the pond empty? A survey sheet would simply score it as a zero.
scenes.visual: A brief recap: the first film's 20-pond map, TEAL and GREY, with the counter p. Zoom into one GREY-looking pond. An observer cartoon visits three times; three tick boxes fill in: 0, 0, 0. A question mark.
scenes.narration: Sources, rescue and corridors all rest on one record: which ponds are occupied. Three visits, no toads heard. Is the pond empty? A survey sheet would simply score it as a zero.

scenes.tts: A zero on a survey sheet has two meanings. The pond may truly be empty. Or toads were there, and the observer missed them on every visit.
scenes.visual: The pond splits into two cut-away panels, both with history '000'. Left: empty water, label 'empty'. Right: a toad hidden among the reeds, pond drawn TEAL with dashed outline, label 'occupied, missed three times'. Schematic.
scenes.narration: A zero on a survey sheet has two meanings. The pond may truly be empty. Or toads were there, and the observer missed them on every visit.

scenes.tts: So surveyors return to each site several times in one season, while occupancy is assumed not to change. Each visit scores a one for detected, and a zero for not.
scenes.visual: A calendar strip for one breeding season with three visit dates. Over each date, a tick box fills with 1 or 0. Label: 'occupancy fixed within the season'.
scenes.narration: So surveyors return to each site several times in one season, while occupancy is assumed not to change. Each visit scores a one for detected, and a zero for not.

scenes.tts: Three visits give a history, like one one zero, or zero one zero. A zero one zero history shows a pond that was occupied, and missed twice.
scenes.caption: Three visits give a history, like 110, or 010. A 010 history shows a pond that was occupied, and missed twice.
scenes.visual: Several ponds, each with three tick boxes: '110', '010', '100', '000'. The '010' pond lights TEAL; its two 0 boxes get small labels 'missed'.
scenes.narration: Three visits give a history, like 110, or 010. A 010 history shows a pond that was occupied, and missed twice.

scenes.tts: Take eight ponds that really hold toads. Each visit detects them with a probability of one half, independently of the other visits. After three visits, how many ponds look empty?
scenes.visual: Eight TEAL ponds with dashed outlines in a row, each with three blank tick boxes. On-screen: 'detection per visit = 0.5', '3 visits'. A question mark over the row.
scenes.narration: Take eight ponds that really hold toads. Each visit detects them with a probability of one half, independently of the other visits. After three visits, how many ponds look empty?

scenes.visual: The eight ponds wait; small countdown 5 to 1.

scenes.tts: About one, on average. With independent visits, three misses in a row happen one time in eight. Each extra visit halves that chance again.
scenes.visual: Expected tally, not a random run (computed): at detection 0.5 the eight three-visit histories are equally likely, so the boxes fill with one of each: '110', '011', '101', '010', '111', '100', '001', '000'. The '000' pond stays dashed and looks empty. On-screen: '0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.125 = 1 in 8', and a small note: 'expected tally; in any one set of eight the number of 000 ponds varies'. A fourth box appears: '0.5^4 = 0.0625'.
scenes.narration: About one, on average. With independent visits, three misses in a row happen one time in eight. Each extra visit halves that chance again.

scenes.tts: Harder species are missed more often. When each visit finds them only three times in ten, about one occupied pond in three comes out all zeros.
scenes.caption: Harder species are missed more often. When each visit finds them only 3 times in 10, about 1 occupied pond in 3 comes out all zeros.
scenes.visual: The same eight ponds at detection 0.3, shown as an expected tally (computed): on average about three of them read '000' (8 × 0.343 = 2.7). On-screen: '0.7 × 0.7 × 0.7 = 0.343, about 1 in 3'.
scenes.narration: Harder species are missed more often. When each visit finds them only 3 times in 10, about 1 occupied pond in 3 comes out all zeros.

scenes.tts: No single site can settle it, but many sites together can. Across them, the pattern of histories carries the answer. A model estimates the chance of detection and the fraction occupied, together.
scenes.visual: A grid of 40 ponds with histories. Ponds with any 1 light TEAL. Two dials build beside the grid: 'detection per visit' and 'fraction occupied, p'. Arrows run from the histories into both dials.
scenes.narration: No single site can settle it, but many sites together can. Across them, the pattern of histories carries the answer. A model estimates the chance of detection and the fraction occupied, together.

scenes.tts: A naive count lights only the ponds with a detection. The corrected estimate is higher, because some silent ponds hold toads. Treat every silent pond as empty, and occupancy is counted low.
scenes.visual: Two bars side by side: GREY bar 'naive: ponds with any detection' and a taller TEAL bar 'corrected: estimated fraction occupied'. A few '000' ponds on the grid turn dashed TEAL. Schematic.
scenes.narration: A naive count lights only the ponds with a detection. The corrected estimate is higher, because some silent ponds hold toads. Treat every silent pond as empty, and occupancy is counted low.

scenes.tts: Darryl MacKenzie and colleagues published this method. They tested it on volunteer surveys of wetlands in Maryland, made two years earlier.
scenes.visual: Name card 'MacKenzie and colleagues, Ecology, 2002'. A simple outline of Maryland with wetland dots; label 'volunteer surveys, 2000'. A cartoon American toad.
scenes.narration: Darryl MacKenzie and colleagues published this method. They tested it on volunteer surveys of wetlands in Maryland, made two years earlier.

scenes.tts: American toads were detected at least once at only about a third of the wetlands analysed. The model put the fraction occupied near one half.
scenes.visual: Bars for the toads: GREY 'detected: 10 / 29 = 0.34' and TEAL 'estimated occupied: 0.49'. The gap between them is shaded with small hidden-toad icons, label 'there, never heard'.
scenes.narration: American toads were detected at least once at only about a third of the wetlands analysed. The model put the fraction occupied near one half.

scenes.tts: The method has rules of its own. Occupancy must stay fixed across a season's visits. Toads must never be recorded where they are absent. And detection must be independent among sites and among visits.
scenes.visual: Three checklist cards appear one at a time beside the grid: 'occupancy fixed within the season', 'no false detections', 'detection independent among sites and visits'. Each gets a TEAL tick.
scenes.narration: The method has rules of its own. Occupancy must stay fixed across a season's visits. Toads must never be recorded where they are absent. And detection must be independent among sites and among visits.

scenes.tts: So a zero is a result of looking, not proof of absence. How hard you looked belongs in the analysis, before any pond is called empty.
scenes.visual: Back to the single pond and its '000' history. The two panels from earlier, 'empty' and 'occupied, missed', sit side by side, with a magnifying glass over the history labelled 'how hard did you look?'.
scenes.narration: So a zero is a result of looking, not proof of absence. How hard you looked belongs in the analysis, before any pond is called empty.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Take-home line: 'A survey zero is a result of looking, not proof of absence.'
